en: Always stay outside Mayon Volcano's six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone to avoid deadly ash falls and lava flows.
If you feel a strong earthquake near the Philippine Sea, immediately move to higher ground to escape a tsunami.
Never swim in the Cagayan River during the rainy season because sudden flash floods can sweep you away.
Drink plenty of water during May in Metro Manila, as the high heat index can cause heatstroke.
Wear long pants when hiking Mt. Pulag's mossy forests to protect your skin from leech bites and infections.
Residents of Eastern Visayas must prepare strong roofs because this region faces the Pacific Ocean and receives the most typhoons.
Avoid swimming in the Pasig River because high levels of water pollution can cause severe skin infections and diseases.
Always wear a helmet when exploring the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River to protect your head from low cave ceilings.
Wear water shoes when walking on coral reefs in Tubbataha to prevent painful cuts from sharp marine life.
Pack warm jackets when visiting Baguio City in December, because its high elevation makes the climate very cold.
Wear an N95 mask during a Taal Volcano eruption to prevent fine volcanic ash from damaging your lungs.
Always boil water from the Agusan River before drinking to kill harmful bacteria and prevent severe stomach illnesses.
